mentions.excerpt: CoreWeave rose 19 percent on what a bear called “banner revenue”.
On CNBC, CoreWeave’s chief executive said the company was renting out 2020-vintage GPUs on contracts running to 2029 at full freight.
Depressed valuations for Oracle and CoreWeave were already pricing that discomfort.
CoreWeave wrote debt covenants against an OpenAI contract.
A local moratorium may change the map without changing demand, as CoreWeave management said on its second-quarter call.
CoreWeave offers the strongest case against a simple depreciation story.

Kakashii’s figures are spectacular: CoreWeave revenue rose from $229 million in 2023 to $5.1 billion in 2025, active power from about 70 megawatts to more than 1.5 gigawatts, and backlog to $104.2 billion.
CoreWeave priced a convertible at a 2.875% coupon, up from 1.75% in April, and made the deal bigger.
Nvidia now gives investment-grade customers a year to pay, up from 90 days, and some CoreWeave loan covenants tie to its OpenAI contract.
CoreWeave’s convertible coupon rose from 1.75% in April to 2.875% on a larger September deal.

CoreWeave is a contract-financed infrastructure company whose assets become technologically obsolete much faster than the buildings it leases, whose largest customers are competing clouds, and whose only GPU supplier is also an investor, customer…
CoreWeave and Nvidia's efforts to show stamina in the pricing of their chips are simply at odds with the depreciation realities lenders actually face.
